mines.mine_notes: Flagship open-pit mine, Krasnoyarsk region (Eastern Siberia). Per Polyus public operating results (polyus.com, 2H/FY2025 release, March 2026): 2025 refined gold 926.5 koz vs 1,265.7 koz in 2024 (-27%), on planned lower grades; decline expected to last to ~2028. Production figure cited for context only — field left blank per stub policy.

Open-pit mine, Krasnoyarsk region (Eastern Siberia). Per Polyus public operating results: 2025 refined gold 434.0 koz vs 500.3 koz in 2024. Production figure cited for context only — field left blank per stub policy.

Open-pit mine, Magadan region (Far East). Per Polyus public operating results: 2025 refined gold 567.4 koz vs 455.6 koz in 2024 (+25%). Production figure cited for context only — field left blank per stub policy.

Open-pit mine, Irkutsk region (Eastern Siberia). Per Polyus public operating results: 2025 refined gold 271.7 koz vs 242.2 koz in 2024 (+12%), including refined gold from Sukhoi Log pilot processing at the Verninskoye mill. Production figure cited for context only — field left blank per stub policy.

Open-pit heap-leach mine, North-Eastern Siberia (Sakha Republic/Yakutia). Per Polyus public operating results: 2025 refined gold 329.7 koz vs 326.8 koz in 2024 (+1%). Production figure cited for context only — field left blank per stub policy.

Placer (alluvial) gold operations. Per Polyus public operating results: 2025 gold from the Razdolinskoye, Ugakhan and Radostnoye deposits was 16.5 koz, reflected in the consolidated financial statements as a capitalized item (excluded from refined-gold output totals). Figure cited for context only — field left blank per stub policy.

Flagship development project, Irkutsk region (Eastern Siberia). Per polyus.com: 43.5 Moz proven & probable gold reserves. Target full operation 2029; planned to roughly double group output toward ~6 Moz by 2030; project capex ~US$6B. 2025 capex record US$2.2B largely Sukhoi Log. Figures cited for context only — fields left blank per stub policy.
Development project, Irkutsk region (Eastern Siberia). Per polyus.com: 3.1 Moz proven & probable gold reserves. Figure cited for context only — field left blank per stub policy.
Development project, Khabarovsk region (Far East). Per polyus.com: 3.0 Moz proven & probable gold reserves. Figure cited for context only — field left blank per stub policy.

notes: Polyus PJSC is Russia's largest gold producer and is under US/UK/EU sanctions (Western bans on Russian gold imports since 2022); RING ETF carries it as a 0.00% legacy holding. No English FY2025 annual report is publicly accessible, so all numeric fields are null. Figures quoted in mine_notes are Polyus company-disclosed public operating results (polyus.com 'Operating and financial results for the second half of 2025 and full year 2025', March 2026) and the polyus.com operations page, given for context only and flagged as unverified: group 2025 total gold output 2,528.8 koz (-16% YoY), refined gold 2,529.3 koz, revenue US$8.7B (+19%), EBITDA US$6.35B; 2026 production guidance 2.5-2.6 Moz.
